newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close firmer on rebound in property shrs.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close firmer on rebound in property shrs.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed firmer on Monday, boosted chiefly by a rebound in property developers and despite the sharp weakness seen on Wall Street last week, brokers said.
"A lot of people can only see clear blue sky ahead," said Adrian Ngan, director at Peregrine Securities. "More people here seem to think interest rates will remain unchanged."

The Hang Seng Index closed 46.45 points, or 0.33 percent, higher at 14,108.82 after touching a low of 13,946.94 early in the morning session. Turnover was a hefty HK$11.56 billion, slightly less than Friday's HK$12.73 billion.
Not all brokers were so sanguine.
"We think the Fed will raise rates tomorrow," said James Robertson, vice president at Salomon Brothers. "We believe the Fed will tighten quite aggressively over the year."

On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 138.88 points, or 1.89 percent, to 7.194.67 on renewed worries the U.S. economy was growing too fast and an interest rate hike was inevitable at the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.
Brokers said local investors in Hong Kong were only looking at the very short term.
Property stocks led the market. Developers Cheung Kong and Sun Hung Kai Properties topped the most active list.

"The market saw a recovery signal in Sun Hung Kai's Property sales on Sunday," said Sam Luk, dealing director at core Pacific Securities. "People are hoping Cheung Kong's sale this week will show higher prices than the last two to three months."
Cheung Kong jumped to a new all time high of HK$79.25, before easing to close HK$1.75 higher at HK$79.00 on heavy turnover of HK$615.40 million.
"Pre-sale programmes are going much better than I had expected," said Peregrine's Ngan.
"But valuations are still getting a little stretched."
Sun Hung Kai Properties leaped HK$2.25 to close at HK$96.00 on trade of HK$596.76 million.
Hongkong Telecom added HK$0.10 to HK$15.65.
"There are few sellers (of Telecom)," said Luk, adding he expected the share to maintain a steady uptrend despite any volatility in the market.
Fund management house Regent Pacific debuted at HK$2.80 on Monday, then eased to close at HK$2.60 on trade of HK$156.58 million. The shares were offered at HK$2.62 per share.
